documents.title: Guidelines for the Georgetown Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: A university-wide landing page from University Information Services and Counsel with six principles (accountability, transparency, fairness, privacy, security, IP) and two cautions on bots and unapproved tools. It is mostly about data and tool use and says little about coursework.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set principles ('accountable for the work product', disclosure 'if prescribed by law, university policy') and data rules but say nothing on whether students may use AI in coursework, so no stance is set and decisions fall to other policies.

documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance on writing course AI policies, with sample syllabus language, faculty examples (including a Computer Science one), per-assignment wording, a policy on AI-assisted grading, and an FAQ on detection and escalation.
